title: Two Palestinian teenagers killed in al-Mughayyir; Israeli military and local officials dispute cause
dek: Palestinian officials say Israeli settlers and soldiers killed teenagers Omar al-Nassan, 19, and Khalil Abu Alia, 16, in the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir on September 3. The Israeli military says its forces fired on Palestinians throwing stones during a security operation to retrieve livestock. The incident reflects escalating West Bank violence and disputed accountability.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Two Palestinian teenagers were killed in al-Mughayyir on September 3; Palestinians and Israeli officials offer conflicting accounts of the circumstances.
bottom_line: The al-Mughayyir incident and Khirbet al-Tabban demolition on the same day underscore the competing Palestinian and Israeli narratives of violence and accountability in the occupied West Bank. No investigation outcomes or accountability measures are named in current reporting; follow whether the deaths generate formal inquiries, arrests, or court proceedings.
body: Two Palestinian teenagers, Omar al-Nassan, 19, and Khalil Abu Alia, 16, were killed in the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir on September 3. The village council told the BBC that the teenagers were killed as they tried to stop Israeli settlers stealing sheep and that confrontations broke out. The Israeli military stated that its forces had entered the village to provide security for an Israeli civilian and police trying to retrieve livestock, and said forces fired on and struck what it called "key instigators" of a "violent disturbance" in which Palestinians threw stones at its troops.

The killing adds to a documented pattern of violence in the occupied West Bank. The UN has recorded more than three settler attacks per day on average so far this year, per BBC reporting. Al-Mughayyir, near Ramallah, has seen repeated settler attacks. WhatsApp messages in groups used by settlers have indicated, according to the BBC's reporting, that they hope to force al-Mughayyir's population to move.

At least 81 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to UN figures cited by the BBC. At least 23 of those deaths have occurred in the context of settler attacks, per the same accounting. By contrast, three Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN.

The broader context includes a police arrest Thursday of a 19-year-old settler on suspicion of participating in an attack on the Palestinian village of Qusra on Saturday. The BBC reports this marks the first settler arrest in weeks of attacks on Qusra. In that incident, dozens of masked settlers descended on Qusra, surrounding a house while Palestinians were trapped inside and throwing stones. Israeli soldiers deployed to Qusra detained the trapped Palestinians but not the settlers, allowing them to leave, according to reporting; the Israeli military said troops at Qusra removed "rioters" and protected residents.

On the same day as the al-Mughayyir killings, September 3, Israeli forces demolished the Palestinian village of Khirbet al-Tabban in the Masafer Yatta area. The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem said the village's 70 residents, including 28 children, were given no warning prior to the demolition and were not allowed to remove their property. B'Tselem described the demolition as the most significant in Masafer Yatta since May 2025.

The demolition context: In the 1980s, the Israeli military declared about 3,000 hectares in the South Hebron Hills, which includes Masafer Yatta, as a restricted firing zone for training purposes. The Israeli military says the Palestinian homes in the firing zone have been built illegally. In 2022, Israel's Supreme Court ruled to allow the demolition of homes in the firing zone and the expulsion of their residents. Palestinian residents had argued that demolition and expulsion violated international law and that their families had been living there since before the State of Israel was established.

B'Tselem says Khirbet al-Tabban is the 66th Palestinian community to be expelled by Israeli authorities since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023. B'Tselem alleges that the expulsions and demolitions are part of a campaign of "ethnic cleansing" being carried out in the West Bank. The Israeli military has faced mounting criticism for actively participating in settler attacks on Palestinians, standing by, or failing to prosecute those responsible, according to reporting.

Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside Israeli settlers in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. The settlements are illegal under international law.
